newsitem.title: UK: Russia tipped as best performer in 1997 - survey.
newsitem.headline: Russia tipped as best performer in 1997 - survey.

text.p: Russia remains the most widely tipped emerging market for outperformance in 1997 among fund managers, a survey released on Thursday said.

It said widespread optimism seen in the last quarter of 1996 towards emerging markets had been sustained in the first quarter of this year, with Latin America and eastern Europe the most favoured regions relative to South East Asia.
The report commissioned by consultants Burson-Marsteller said three key themes had been identified by fund managers in 1997;
- increased liquidity in world markets as global investors look for better returns outside the lower yielding domestic equity and developed market instrument,
- the beneficial impact of a slight U.S. interest rate correction due to increased capital inflow, and
- the continuing privatisation process, mostly in Latin America and in Brazil specifically.

The quarterly survey covers institutions managing over 80 percent of the total value held in global emerging market equity funds and 70 percent of all portfolio investment into emerging markets from the developed world.
It said Latin American markets offered the possibility of decreased interest rates, a major privatisation programme and lower inflation.

"These markets, once seen as a bellwether of the U.S. economy, are now believed to be able to weather the storm of a correction in either U.S. interest rates and/or the U.S. stockmarket," the report said.
Brazil and Mexico are favoured in the region, with Chile likely to be "a quiet success story" and Argentina and Peru viewed more neutrally.
Eastern Europe is seen offering the best valuations.
"Despite (Russian President Boris) Yeltsin's health problems and concerns about political stability, Russia remains widely favoured."
Outside Russia, Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary are the key markets. The smaller Slovakia, Ukraine and Croatia are attracting interest as investors seek better returns.
Asia Pacific markets are seen experiencing structural difficulties in some markets, it said.

Malaysia and Indonesia are seen good long term bets despite the latter's recent political problems. India, despite perceived problems with accounting standards and settlements, and China are being viewed increasingly positively by some fund managers.

The report also said that the attitude to corporate governance and shareholder value by emerging market companies were increasingly impacting on the investment approach of global investors although total acceptance of these issues was felt to be a long way off.
But increasing competition for international capital would see companies not delivering shareholder value down-rated by investors.
